land.text: Karakorum and the Mongolian heartland in Ariq Böke's charge since 1258

capitals.name: Karakorum
capitals.note: Ariq Böke's kurultai at Karakorum proclaimed him Great Khan; Karakorum 'changed hands twice during the war' (Ariq Böke page) and he 'retreated from Karakorum' in late 1260 (Toluid page). No page names a later seat, so the dot stays at Karakorum.

correction.text: Karakorum and the Mongolian heartland, which Ariq Böke 'controlled while his brothers campaigned abroad'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: a civil-war claimant has no Cliopatria row (the Mongol Empire row covers the whole). The Toluid page: Ariq had Karakorum, 'the empire's capital, which Möngke had placed him in charge of in 1258'. Outer Mongolia is the researcher's reading of 'the Mongolian heartland'.

correction.text: what is left after Kublai takes 'most of Mongolia' by 1261: the west of Mongolia and the Yenisei valley, 'Ariq's Yenisei Valley supply line'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, low certainty: the pages say Kublai held most of Mongolia by 1261 and that Ariq's supply line ran to the Yenisei valley; neither names the land Ariq held 1262-64, so this is a bridging reading (Khakassia stands for the Yenisei valley). The Ili was Ariq's only briefly (occupation 1263-64, see ulus-of-chagatai).

ledger.note: 1260: Ariq Böke is proclaimed Great Khan at Karakorum. Kublai was elected at Kaiping in May 1260 'where he was elected Great Khan'; Ariq Böke's kurultai in Karakorum proclaimed him Great Khan 'a month later', creating two rival claimants; the Ariq page has him elected in 1259 while his brothers were absent and gives the infobox reign 11 August 1259 to 21 August 1264.

region.text: the Mongolian heartland of the civil war

ledger.note: 1260: the Toluid Civil War begins. Infobox 'Date: 1260-1264'; Kublai's army advanced toward Karakorum in late 1260. The Mongol Empire dossier opens the same contest over the Mongolian heartland in 1260.

1260: Ariq Böke names Alghu head of the Chagatai ulus. 'In 1260 Alghu was appointed as head of the ulus of the Chagatai Khanate by the Great Khan claimant' Ariq Böke; Ariq also gave Alghu control of the tax revenues of the region (Toluid page).

1261: Kublai holds most of Mongolia. 'By 1261, most of Mongolia was now under the control of Kublai' after Ariq Böke lost at Shimultai (1261) and 'retreated from Karakorum' (late 1260); Karakorum changed hands twice (Ariq page).
1262: Alghu turns on Ariq Böke. 'In 1262 he rebelled against Ariq Boke and commanded 150,000 soldiers against him' (Alghu page); he 'executed Ariq's envoys' and declared for Kublai in 1263.

1263: Ariq Böke takes the Ili from Alghu. Alghu 'was forced to flee to Samarkand in 1263' after Ariq Böke attacked him and Ariq 'devastated the Ili region'; 'lost Almalikh to Ariq' (Toluid page). Mirrors the ulus-of-chagatai ledger.
1264: Ariq Böke gives up the Ili with his surrender. 'traveled to Shangdu alone and surrendered to Kublai in 1264, ending the civil war'.
1264: Ariq Böke surrenders at Shangdu and the Toluid Civil War ends. 'Ariq Böke finally submitted to Kublai in 1264' (Ariq page); infobox reign ends 21 August 1264.

region.text: what was left of Ariq Böke's holdings

ledger.note: 1264: the rebel claimant is crushed. 'Ariq Böke finally submitted to Kublai in 1264'; imprisoned, he 'died mysteriously a few years after his surrender' (1266, Toluid page).

wars.name: Toluid Civil War
wars.outcome: Kublai Khan won. Ariq Böke lost at Shimultai (1261), was abandoned by Alghu (1262-63) and surrendered at Shangdu in 1264; he died in custody in 1266. Berke (Golden Horde) backed Ariq, Hulagu backed Kublai but both were busy with their own war.

certainty.note: Court, steppe and oasis frontiers; no line is recorded.

sources.title: Toluid Civil War
sources.note: Toluid Civil War 1260-1264: two kurultais, Karakorum, Shimultai 1261, Alghu, surrender at Shangdu 1264.

sources.title: Ariq Böke
sources.note: Ariq Boke: election 1259/1260, Karakorum and the heartland, Alghu episode, surrender 1264; infobox reign 11 August 1259 to 21 August 1264.

sources.title: Alghu
sources.note: Alghu: appointed head of the Chagatai ulus by Ariq in 1260; rebelled in 1262; allegiance to Kublai 1263.

sources.title: Chagatai Khanate
sources.note: Alghu fled to Samarkand in 1263 after Ariq Boke attacked him; Ariq devastated the Ili.

notes:
A civil-war claimant, not a state with Cliopatria rows: drawn hatched in its own colour (type rebel) from the kurultai at Karakorum in 1260 until the surrender in August 1264. Both successor and predecessor are the Mongol Empire, whose dossier already opens and closes the 1260-1264 contest with the counterpart string 'Ariq Böke' (this dossier's slug is ariq-boke; the colour agent should link the two).

The territory is thin: the pages name Karakorum and the Mongolian heartland (1260), say Kublai held most of Mongolia by 1261, mention the Yenisei valley only as a supply line, and have Ariq take Almalikh from Alghu in 1263. The 1261-1264 keyframe is a bridging reading; a gap-filler could open the Kublai Khan and Mongol Empire pages for where Ariq's court wintered 1261-1263 (Western Mongolia and the Yenisei valley are the guess). Disagreements: infobox reign 11 August 1259 (Ariq page) versus a kurultai a month after Kublai's of May 1260 (Toluid page); Karakorum changed hands twice (Ariq page) but the Toluid page has only the late-1260 retreat.
